name: Room-temperature cell bank
subtitle: a cell bank that needs no liquid nitrogen

effects.effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out
an egg can be fertilized outside the body

effect: certain proteins turn glassy inside cells and let them survive drying out
how: Cell therapies, fertility samples and research lines all live in tanks of liquid nitrogen, and a week of failed resupply or a power cut during a storm destroys decades of work. Drying is the alternative, but cells die as the last water leaves and their structures collide. Cells given the tardigrade proteins that turn their insides to glass can be dried and kept in a sealed vial on a shelf, then woken with water.
obstacle: Mammalian cells have so far survived the drying but not the long wait, and nobody knows what fraction wakes after a year.
why: Drying works briefly in culture; long dry storage of human cells is unproven.
real: CAHS proteins protect HeLa and insect cells against osmotic/desiccation stress and gel reversibly on drying, but the EU DRYLIFE project concluded dry-state mammalian cells need many further changes, and no dried-and-revived mammalian cell bank was found.
